seo_title: What Do Koreans Buy at an Olive Young Sale? A VIP Shopper's Cart
dek: A shopper who normally buys at department stores empties an Olive Young cart during sale week — and viewers order the same items on the app before the video ends.

takeaway.why_korea: Olive Young's sale calendar sets the rhythm of Korean beauty buying, and creators race to publish 'what I actually repurchase' lists on day one of the sale. This one works because it is framed against luxury counters — a shopper who normally buys department-store brands says the Olive Young picks beat them — and because the cart mixes skincare with makeup, so it reads like a real basket rather than a sponsorship list.
takeaway.best_for: Restocking basics: a micellar cleanser, a ceramide body-and-face cream, toner pads, and a tint and mascara that survive a Korean summer.
takeaway.skip_if: You are building a routine from zero or want actives. This is a repurchase haul, not a regimen.

products.why: Micellar water she repurchases; the comment consensus is that it needs a second cleanse.
The winter saviour a commenter credits for cracked, wind-burned arms and legs.
Sale-day pad restock; commenters say they waited for the discount to buy it.
The lip that sells out whenever she shows it — viewers blame her for the stockouts.
Summer-proof mascara pick; comments recommend pairing it with Clio's own remover.

sentiment.method: editorial review of 80 top comments, weighted by likes
sentiment.note: Purchase-intent comments dominate — people report ordering the cart minutes after watching. The single most-liked comment is a detailed packaging complaint about one tint.

quote_specs.en: I watched this and ordered the whole list on the Olive Young app for same-day delivery — it just arrived. What a world.
Illiyoon's ceramide cream at 3:37 is my winter saviour. My arms and legs crack and sting in the cold wind, and the wrong body lotion only makes it worse.
Unnie, the Clio mascara, the cheek, the lip — everything you showed is sold out because of you. Just launch your own channel already.
I just bought the dried squid strips at Olive Young and the portion is far too small for the price...
quote_specs.note: Off-topic but real: Olive Young sells snacks, and the comment section treats the store as a general shop.

caveat: Illiyoon's ceramide cream is rich — acne-prone skin should try it on the body first. Bioderma's micellar water is not a sunscreen remover on its own; the videos in this genre consistently pair it with a foam cleanse.
body: The interesting thing about this haul is the comparison it makes. She shops department-store counters normally and says so up front; the Olive Young basket is the test of whether a 20,000-won product does the same job as a 90,000-won one. Twelve items later, the answer is mostly yes — with skincare taking the top half and colour makeup taking the bottom.

The skincare half is a restock list rather than a discovery list: Bioderma's micellar water, Torriden's hyaluronic serum, La Roche-Posay B5 and Bioderma Cicabio as repair creams, Illiyoon's ceramide cream, and Rejuran toner pads. The makeup half is where the sale behaviour shows — Rom&nd's Juicy Lasting Tint, Clio's Kill Lash mascara, Lilybyred's water tint — the products Korean viewers buy in multiples when the discount opens.

What the comments reveal is how fast this converts. One of the top comments is a viewer who ordered the entire list through Olive Young's same-day delivery while the video was still playing. Another, the most-liked of all, is a precise complaint that Lilybyred's tint is missing a gasket in its cap — the kind of defect report that only a comment section of regular buyers produces.
